acceptanceCriteria.statement: When a tour leg targets a body occluded by another body (classically a moon on the far side of its parent planet), the ship reaches the target and captures it, instead of pinning against the occluding body's collision barrier and aborting. The path clears the obstacle's surface.

verifyVia.input: Live (chrome-devtools :9223, tab foreground): drive a HELM tour (or _lab tour with the drive engaged) in a system with moons; identify a leg whose target moon starts on the far side of its parent planet (segment ship->moon crosses the planet); run the tour telemetry sampler across that leg.
verifyVia.observable: distReal to the target closes monotonically to capture and the leg ends in HOLD (arrival), NOT stallAbort; the ship is never parked at ~1.05*R of the occluding body with speed~0 for the leg; the min-cap 'nearBody' during the leg is not a non-target obstacle held at surf~0.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Over a full multi-body tour in a system that includes moons, the ship visibly travels between stops and stall-aborts stay near zero — no self-sustaining 'select -> sit still -> reselect' carousel. Consecutive legs do not share the same pinned ship position.

verifyVia.input: Live (:9223): run a complete HELM tour (star + planets + moons) end-to-end with the telemetry sampler installed; compare against the 2026-07-01 triage baseline (35 aborts) captured in the same harness.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The supercruise drive does not silently drop mid-tour (near big stars or anywhere) and strand the ship at a sublight crawl. If a legitimate proximity condition would drop the drive during a hands-off tour, the tour keeps making supercruise progress (the drop is prevented for the autopilot, or the drive re-engages) so the ship never gets stuck at ~0.0015 u/s.
